None in the tree. The 14 files are Rust sources, manifests, lock files, .gitignore and the one sample.

inspiration: Tooling, not visuals: one archive file holds many named entries, with a directory table giving each entry's name and offset, and each entry compressed on its own. If we ever need a pack format for our own assets, this layout is a clean reference for the idea (we write our own code).

The command-line shape is simple: one archive argument plus subcommands to list entries and stream one out, so an asset can be checked without unpacking the whole pack. Worth copying for our own asset tools.
The reader is a library crate and the command-line tool is a separate crate that depends on it, so other tools can reuse the reader. A workspace layout to copy for our tooling.
There is no art, sound, map or creature here to recreate. The sample archive is game data with no licence and should not be used as a reference for the look of anything.
